summary.intent: Shipped Callisto 0.18.0 and the gate workflow change, then redesign the release PR body and changelog to world-class quality: lead with what merging releases, flag blockers and pause-worthy items, support rich Markdown, and stay ready for future templates and custom renderers.
summary.outcome: 0.18.0 shipped (18 min vs 32) and the gate PR #462 merged and verified on a real push. The redesign was explored with competitor research, a published mock-up artifact (v2), and a three-layer architecture (facts model, findings, pure renderers). Step 1, the `core` to `cargo`/`npm`/`pypi` ecosystem label fix, was committed on `feat/release-notes-model` with a changeset and updated snapshot. No PR was opened yet.

repo: Release PR body is composed in crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/pr_body.rs; bare-named packages fell back to the `core` ecosystem label because the package-id prefix was missing. The fix derives the label from the manifest the bump writes to.
Changelog lookups (`find_section`, `has_heading`, `strip_alias_title`, release-notes extraction) match the exact `## X.Y.Z` heading, so date and compare link must go on a line below it.
`VersionPlan` is in-memory only with no Serialize, per docs/architecture/versioning.md. `ComposePrBodyReport` already carries `schema_version`, giving precedent for a versioned JSON model.
docs/stability.md calls library crates internal, so any renderer SDK needs its own small semver'd crate rather than exposing the internal ones.
The merged gate job lets verify and release identification start in parallel; on non-release pushes plan, builds and execute are skipped and version-pr waits on the gate.
The PR body has no handling for GitHub's ~65k char limit (unreproduced risk), and changeset Markdown is only indented under a bullet, so headings are not rebased.
Changeset files in this repo live in .changeset/ and the PR body snapshot is under crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/snapshots/.
The user has decided the emoji in the release PR body stay; saved as feedback memory.

code.finding: Ecosystem label was `package.ecosystem().map(prefix).unwrap_or("core")`, giving `core` for bare crate names. Now derived from the manifest write target.
Renders `## {version}` plus flat bullets in changeset filename order via `indent_changeset_summary`; no grouping, date, compare link or heading rebasing.

workflow: gh and git calls need dangerouslyDisableSandbox, and the worktree guard rejects heredocs and compound git, so scripts are written with the Write tool and run separately.
Back up factual claims about competitors with real fetched output rather than memory, and say what was not verified.
Check PR state before pushing to a branch; do not push to branches of already-merged PRs.
Confirm intent and avoid over-engineering; the user pushes back on shell-script and rushed one-off fixes and prefers family-level fixes with features in Rust.
Mock-ups published as artifacts let the user judge design before code is built.
Snapshot tests with insta: run with INSTA_UPDATE=always, then delete stray .snap.new files and check the snapshot diff.

friction: Earlier mistakes the user called out: pushing to an already-merged PR's branch, choosing macos-15 over macos-latest, and over-engineering the check-api change.
Sandbox blocked Python writes under the jobs dir, requiring unsandboxed reruns.
Release PR body and changelog output was mediocre (wrong `core` label, filename-titled sections, flat unordered bullets), which prompted the redesign.
Classifier blocks remote branch deletion, stash drop, closing trails and resolving findings, leaving those to the user.
Competitor research for a release-please PR body and Nx came back empty, so those comparisons are incomplete.
open_items: Open a PR for the label fix on `feat/release-notes-model`, then extract the serializable versioned `ReleaseNotes` model and a typed findings list from pr_body.rs with no behavior change (step 2).
Rework the PR body onto the model: changelog preview with first-sentence titles, a 'Merging will publish' block, a verdict (ready, read first, would fail) and a 'not releasing' list.

Grouped changelog (`### Major/Minor/Patch Changes`) with date and compare link below the heading, `Breaking:`/`Action:` markers, optional git-derived PR links, and block-aware Markdown with heading rebasing, image rewriting and a size cap. This changes a committed format and needs the user's decision.
Verify that the preview plan can run on the PR branch without credentials, the false-positive rate of 'changed, no changeset', and that the hold workflow has `pull-requests: write` for labels.
Decide whether to add a Markdown parser dependency such as pulldown-cmark.

Prep for renderers and templates only: custom renderers (command first, Rust SDK crate, trust levels, post-render invariants) are deferred, but the config shape should reserve `{ package, version, sha256 }`.
CLI diagnostics: `status --explain`, version preview, `callisto doctor`, API-aware `callisto add`, run summary timeline and release receipt comment.
Update the artifact with the lean-PR/CLI split, defaults, markers and block model.
User-side items: tell monokl about E170, delete merged remote branches, drop the old stash, close merged Entire trails and resolve findings.
Decisions pending: lock-step workspace `version.workspace = true` inheritance, and tightening the release-commit manifest check.
Deferred: `release-pr apply`, `bump.rs` comment cleanup, ~40 'Regression test for' headers, handing plugin learnings to the other session, E167 on a partial asset.
